chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: two tape procedures from a fixed bank-exchange network, labels with s<Wm, tau=1-2^-50, interchange and layer recurrences, ring convolution, resampling and chirp, the algorithm, recovery and the time table. B carries the central saving through its mechanism: the exchange B1-B4, the label budget with telescoping and orthonormal bases, eta_b and eta_c, the phase-kernel derivation and the C^{tensor m} endpoint, and the frame identity giving H<-H+D. A only asserts the complex interface (S2.4.3.5) and the endpoint identities, so its chain thins where B's does not.

errors.says: Since Harvey and van der Hoeven reached O(n log n), a further saving must beat a logarithmic factor by a power.
errors.paper: The paper says only that HvdH reached O(n log n) and that it obtains a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor. It does not say that any further saving must be a power saving.

errors.says: The rank-saving recursion gives cost per volume O(e^tau) at parameter e for both the bit network and the complex network (butterfly layers).
errors.paper: Only the bit recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) gives O(e^tau). The complex recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) gives internal costs O(e^lambda), leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and O(d^lambda') in total. B's own S1.4.4.3 states this correctly.

errors.says: Over F_2 every nonzero residual contains a norm-one coordinate unit, so it is nonalternating.
errors.paper: The paper builds a norm-one vector in each residual by tensoring chosen norm-one vectors: coordinate units in some factors, but the triple vectors in the lines P and Q in others. The result is not in general a coordinate unit of the residual.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and the three minor ones do not change the comparison. On the core results B carries essential sub-steps that A only asserts or omits: B1-B4 of the bank exchange, L2-L4 of the label budget, P1, P2 and P4 of the phase interface, M1-M2 of the matrix shear, R2-R3, and the guard-width derivation S1-S5. B's chain also carries the mechanism of the central saving where A's thins out. B is preferred on every item but one, and A is preferred on none.
